summary: Iteration 11 verifies the social-posting intent detection + SYSTEM CONTEXT injection + serialize_mission() field surface added by E1. 13/13 backend pytest tests pass (test_mission_social_intent.py). The three target branches all behave correctly: (A) twitter goal on standing org → social_platform='twitter', has_social_session=True, goal gets the AUTHENTICATED [SYSTEM CONTEXT] block (mentions ALREADY-loaded cookies, MUST publish, PUBLISHED:/FAILED: prefix); (B) linkedin goal on the same org (no linkedin cookies) → social_platform='linkedin', has_social_session=False, goal gets the NO-SESSION block (DO NOT log in, DO NOT ask for credentials, finish with 'FAILED: no login cookies on file for linkedin'); (C) non-social goal ('research top 3 pain management clinics') → social_platform='', has_social_session=False, goal returned VERBATIM with no SYSTEM CONTEXT appended. serialize_mission() round-trips both new fields through GET /orgs/{id}/missions and GET /missions/{id}. _build_lead_mission_system_prompt() now contains the 'LOGIN CREDENTIALS — NEVER ASK' rule + the dedicated 'SOCIAL POSTING' section with PUBLISHED:/FAILED: prefix guidance. Existing test_social_autopost.py (11 tests) still 100% green — no regression on the dedicated autopost scheduler path. Frontend smoke: missions list page renders the augmented goals correctly with the [SYSTEM CONTEXT] block visible, non-social goal stays clean. detect_social_platform_in_goal() handles linkedin/twitter/tweet/facebook/reddit + returns '' for ambiguous + empty input.

critical_code_review_comments: missions.py:1108 detect_social_platform_in_goal is called BEFORE asyncio.create_task (line 1232) so register_mission_storage_state(line 1226) runs synchronously before the loop pops the entry on first browse_url — correct ordering, verified by 200 OK response on social-mission start.

social_autopost.py:572 keyword 'twitter' in 'tweet about our new product' matches via the 'tweet' marker — but a goal like 'twin' or 'twit' would NOT match because 'twitter' is the exact substring. Good — false positives unlikely.

social_autopost.py:559 detect_social_platform_in_goal returns the FIRST matching platform in declaration order (twitter,linkedin,facebook,threads,bluesky,mastodon,reddit). A multi-platform goal like 'post on LinkedIn and tweet about it' will be classified as linkedin (since linkedin appears second in the order list, and twitter would actually win — let me re-verify… markers list has twitter FIRST so 'tweet'/'twitter' wins over 'linkedin' in such a sentence). Either behaviour is acceptable but not documented; consider adding a docstring note for future authors.

missions.py:1140 goal_with_context = body.goal.strip() — leading/trailing whitespace is correctly stripped before appending the context. Original-goal preservation in the prompt is verbatim minus surrounding ws.

MissionCard.js:143-154 the CTA renders only when ALL of: mission.status in ['finished','failed','cancelled'] (via isDone) AND mission.social_platform truthy AND summary starts with 'FAILED:' AND summary matches /login|cookie|session/i. This is correctly tight — won't false-alarm on PUBLISHED missions or non-social ones.

Improvement (low pri): MissionsPage.js list view does NOT use MissionCard component, so the upload-cookies CTA only appears inside chat threads. If a user starts a social mission from outside a chat (via 'Start a mission' button on /app/org/{id}/missions) and it fails with a missing-session, they won't see the recovery CTA on that page. Consider extracting the CTA fragment into a shared <MissionUploadCookiesCTA mission={m}/> component and reusing it in both MissionsPage.js list rows and MissionDetail header.

rca of the issue: Original bug RCA: user-initiated missions for social posting bypassed the autopost scheduler's storage_state injection path → agent's headless browser opened logged-OUT, agent then fell back to ask_user('please give me your LinkedIn login') OR silently drafted the post and finished with 'post is ready for you to manually post'. Fix (verified): missions.start_mission() now (1) calls detect_social_platform_in_goal() to classify the goal, (2) calls load_org_social_storage_state() to merge every social_session for the org into one Playwright storage_state, (3) checks whether any cookie's domain matches the detected platform → has_social_session bool, (4) appends one of two [SYSTEM CONTEXT] blocks to the goal text (authenticated-mode vs no-session-mode), (5) calls register_mission_storage_state(mission_id, merged_state) BEFORE asyncio.create_task so the very first browse_url boots logged-in. The system prompt itself was hardened with NEVER-ASK-FOR-CREDENTIALS + a SOCIAL POSTING section telling the agent to actually publish, not draft-and-handoff.
